question: Does the supreme Lord's teaching posit a separate substrate for the powers?
premises: In the scripture of the supreme Lord no separate substrate is taught for the powers.
The powers are not treated like attributes resting on an unseen principle as in the Kaṇāda system.
This rejects an external bearer for powers conceived as mere properties.
inference: Therefore the powers do not depend on any separate substrate in this teaching.
uncertainties: kāṇādadṛṣṭivat may allude specifically to adṛṣṭa or more broadly to Vaiśeṣika ontology.
plain_english: In the teaching of the supreme Lord, no separate support is claimed for the powers, unlike the Vaiśeṣika view that treats such factors as attributes resting on something else.
